items.title: Read your encryption default and find instance store
items.kills: "Every new EBS volume is encrypted automatically."
items.read_only_alternative: This task is read-only. It needs no alternative.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Read whether EBS encryption by default is turned on in this Region.
steps.expect: EbsEncryptionByDefault with true or false. The value is for this Region only. If it shows true, every new volume that you create in this Region is encrypted. If it shows false, this Region does not enforce encryption, so check the Encrypted field of each new volume.

steps.text: Read the KMS key that EBS encryption uses by default in this Region.
steps.expect: KmsKeyId with alias/aws/ebs, the AWS managed key that EBS creates in each Region. If someone in your account chose a customer managed key, you see the ARN of that key instead.

steps.text: Read the state of block public access for snapshots in this Region.
steps.expect: State with block-all-sharing, block-new-sharing or unblocked. ManagedBy can also show: account, or declarative-policy when a policy of your organization sets the state. Like encryption by default, the setting is for this Region only.

steps.text: Compare two instance types whose names differ by one letter, m5.large and m5d.large. Read whether each type has instance store, and its total size in GB.
steps.command: aws ec2 describe-instance-types --instance-types m5.large m5d.large --query "InstanceTypes[].[InstanceType,InstanceStorageSupported,InstanceStorageInfo.TotalSizeInGB]" --output table
steps.expect: Two rows, in any order. m5.large shows False and no size. m5d.large shows True and a size in GB: the letter d means instance store volumes. If AWS says that a type is not offered in this Region, use c5.large and c5d.large.

items.title: Try to shrink a gp3 volume then grow and retune it
items.kills: "Elastic Volumes can make an over-provisioned volume smaller."
items.cost: More than $0: two small gp3 volumes, 10 GiB together at most, for the minutes that they exist. In the example of the Amazon EBS pricing page, gp3 storage costs $0.08 per GB-month, and IOPS above the free baseline cost $0.005 per provisioned IOPS-month. Billing is in per-second increments, with a 60-second minimum. There is no charge to modify the configuration, but the new size and IOPS are billed after volume modification starts.
items.cost_if_forgotten: More than $0 a day, every day until you delete the volumes: 10 GiB of gp3 storage at $0.08 per GB-month, plus 1,000 IOPS above the baseline at $0.005 per provisioned IOPS-month.
items.read_only_alternative: These commands create nothing. List the volumes of this Region with their size, type and IOPS: aws ec2 describe-volumes --query "Volumes[].[VolumeId,Size,VolumeType,Iops]" --output table Then list the volume modifications of this Region: aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications --query "VolumesModifications[].[VolumeId,OriginalSize,TargetSize,ModificationState]" --output table In each row of the second list, TargetSize is equal to or larger than OriginalSize. If the lists are empty, answer the predict question of step 4 on paper.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Store the name of the first Availability Zone of this Region. Both volumes of this task go there.
steps.expect: No output. AZ now holds a zone name, for example us-east-1a.

steps.text: Create an empty, encrypted gp3 volume of 4 GiB in that zone, tagged for this book and this task. No instance is needed. From here, the volume is billed.
steps.expect: No output. VOL_ID now holds an ID that starts with vol-.

steps.text: Wait until the volume is available.
steps.expect: No output. The prompt comes back when the volume is available.

steps.text: Try to make the volume smaller: ask Elastic Volumes for a size of 2 GiB.
steps.expect: An error about the size. The volume keeps its 4 GiB.
steps.predict: The data on this 4 GiB volume needs only 2 GiB. Can Elastic Volumes make the same volume 2 GiB?
steps.explain: With Elastic Volumes you can [increase the volume size, change the volume type](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-elastic-volumes-modify-without-detach) or adjust the performance. [You can't decrease the volume size](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-volume-size-cannot-decrease) of the same volume. To get a smaller volume, you [create a smaller volume](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-volume-size-cannot-decrease) and copy the data to it with a tool such as rsync.

steps.text: Fix it: create a new 2 GiB gp3 volume in the same zone, with the same tags. On an instance, you would copy the data to the new volume and then delete the old one.
steps.expect: No output. SMALL_ID now holds the ID of the smaller volume.

steps.text: Now use Elastic Volumes in the direction that it allows: grow the first volume to 8 GiB and raise its IOPS to 4,000 in one request. gp3 allows 500 IOPS per GiB, so 8 GiB allows 4,000 IOPS.
steps.expect: A list: modifying, 4, 8, 3000, 4000. The volume started with the gp3 baseline of 3,000 IOPS. The same volume grows in place, and its ID does not change.

steps.text: Read the progress of the change. Run the command again after one minute to see the state move on. Another change to this volume has to wait until the state is completed.
steps.expect: modifying, optimizing or completed, with a progress percentage. From optimizing on, the volume already has its 8 GiB.

cleanup.text: Delete the first volume. If AWS reports an error, wait one minute and run the command again.

verify.expect: An empty list. If an ID still shows, run the command again after one minute.

still_costs: The two volumes, until delete-volume has run for each: a volume is billed for its provisioned size, and the first one also for its extra IOPS, every day until you delete it. If the CloudShell session ended before the cleanup, the variables are empty: find the volumes with the verify command and delete them by their IDs.

If a Recycle Bin retention rule for volumes matches these volumes, a deleted volume stays in the Recycle Bin until the retention period ends, billed at the same rate as a regular volume. List such rules with aws rbin list-rules --resource-type EBS_VOLUME

items.title: Snapshot a volume and restore it in another zone
items.kills: "A snapshot can be restored only in the Availability Zone of its source volume."
items.cost: More than $0: two 2 GiB gp3 volumes and one snapshot, for the minutes that they exist. In the example of the Amazon EBS pricing page, gp3 storage costs $0.08 per GB-month, billed in per-second increments, with a 60-second minimum. The Amazon EBS User Guide names a standard snapshot rate of $0.05 per GB-month, and a snapshot charge is based on the size of the data being backed up: nothing was written to this volume.
items.cost_if_forgotten: More than $0 a day, every day until you delete them: 4 GiB of gp3 storage at $0.08 per GB-month, and the snapshot at $0.05 per GB-month of stored data.
items.read_only_alternative: These commands create nothing. List your own snapshots with their source volume, size and encryption: aws ec2 describe-snapshots --owner-ids self --query "Snapshots[].[SnapshotId,VolumeId,VolumeSize,Encrypted]" --output table Pick one snapshot ID as <SNAP_ID>, and list the volumes that were created from it, with their zones: aws ec2 describe-volumes --filters Name=snapshot-id,Values=<SNAP_ID> --query "Volumes[].[VolumeId,AvailabilityZone,Encrypted]" --output table If the lists are empty, answer the predict question of step 7 on paper.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Store the name of the first Availability Zone of this Region as AZ_A.
steps.expect: No output. AZ_A now holds a zone name, for example us-east-1a.

steps.text: Store the name of a second Availability Zone of the same Region as AZ_B.
steps.expect: No output. AZ_B now holds another zone name, for example us-east-1b. If AZ_B holds None, use a Region with two or more zones.

steps.text: Create an empty, encrypted 2 GiB gp3 volume in AZ_A, tagged for this book and this task. This is the source volume. From here, it is billed.
steps.expect: No output. VOL_ID now holds an ID that starts with vol-.

steps.text: Wait until the volume is available.
steps.expect: No output. The prompt comes back when the volume is available.

steps.text: Take a snapshot of the volume, with the same tags. The volume does not need to be attached to an instance.
steps.expect: No output. SNAP_ID now holds an ID that starts with snap-.

steps.text: Wait until the snapshot is completed. This can take a few minutes.
steps.expect: No output. The prompt comes back when the snapshot is completed.

steps.text: Create a volume from the snapshot in the other zone, AZ_B, with the same tags. Name gp3 as the type: in the CLI, gp2 is the default selection.
steps.expect: No output. NEW_ID now holds an ID that starts with vol-. AWS accepted a zone that differs from the zone of the source volume.
steps.predict: The snapshot comes from a volume in AZ_A. Can you create a volume from it in AZ_B?
steps.explain: Snapshot data is [replicated across all Availability Zones in the Region](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-snapshot-restore-in-any-az-of-region), so you can [restore volumes in any Availability Zones](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-snapshot-restore-in-any-az-of-region) of that Region. A volume and its instance [must be in the same Availability Zone](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-volume-same-az-as-instance). To use the data in another zone, you take a snapshot and [create a duplicate volume in that zone](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-snapshot-restore-volume-other-az). Until the snapshot blocks are [downloaded from Amazon S3 to the new volume](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-volume-initialization-from-snapshot), a restored volume shows [increased I/O latency and decreased performance](../facts/ebs.md#ebs-volume-initialization-from-snapshot).

steps.text: Read the zone, size, encryption and source snapshot of both volumes.
steps.expect: Two rows, in any order. The source volume shows the zone of AZ_A, 2, True and no snapshot ID. The new volume shows the zone of AZ_B, 2, True and SNAP_ID. You set no size and no encryption for the new volume: both came from the snapshot.

cleanup.text: Delete the snapshot. Deleting a snapshot has no effect on the volume.

verify.expect: An empty list. If an ID still shows, run the command again after one minute. Then run the describe-snapshots command of "Still costs money if left": it must also return an empty list.

still_costs: The snapshot, until delete-snapshot has run. Find it with aws ec2 describe-snapshots --owner-ids self --filters Name=tag:task,Values=ebs-t03 --query "Snapshots[].SnapshotId" and delete it by its ID.

The two volumes, until delete-volume has run for each. If the CloudShell session ended before the cleanup, the variables are empty: find the volumes with the verify command and delete them by their IDs.

If a Recycle Bin retention rule for snapshots or volumes matches these resources, a deleted snapshot or volume stays in the Recycle Bin until the retention period ends, billed at the same rate as a regular one. List such rules with aws rbin list-rules --resource-type EBS_SNAPSHOT and again with --resource-type EBS_VOLUME
